name: Name
title: WELCOME TO WARMACHINE AND THE WARCASTER TRAINING GUIDE!

name: Name
body: By downloading the WARMACHINE app, you’ve taken the first step in having the most fun you can have in tabletop miniatures battles. If you’re familiar with WARMACHINE or miniatures games, skip down to USING THE WARMACHINE APP. Otherwise, let’s get you up to speed! Set in the steam-powered world of the Iron Kingdoms, WARMACHINE is a tabletop miniatures game where you get to choose your allegiance, customize an army of models, and engage in epic battles with friends across a tabletop battlefield. Miniatures are hobby models, meaning there is some assembly required and models are supplied unpainted, giving you the opportunity to paint them to your vision of what your army should look like. There are many different armies to choose from in WARMACHINE. If you don’t already have a favorite picked out, you can explore The Forces of WARMACHINE in the app library to get a feel for each different army.

name: Name
body:
Once you’ve found an army that suits your style, we recommend heading to your local game store to grab a Core Army Starter. If you don’t already have a favorite local game store, you can find one close to you using our store finder:
<align=center><font="Poppins-Bold SDF"><color=#79340F>Privateer Press StoreFinder</color></font>
<size=22><font="Roboto-Regular SDF">https://storefinder.privateerpress.com</font></size></align>
If your local game store doesn’t carry WARMACHINE or if you don’t have a store near you, then check out the Privateer Press Online Store—we ship almost everywhere!
<align=center><font="Poppins-Bold SDF"><color=#79340F>Privateer Press Warmachine MkIV Store</color></font>
<size=22><font="Roboto-Regular SDF">https://store.privateerpress.com/games/warmachine-mkiv/</font></size></align>
Once you have an army, you’re ready to dive into everything WARMACHINE has to offer!

name: Name
body:
The WARMACHINE app is your portal to tabletop battles in the Iron Kingdoms. This app provides all the rules and model stat information you need to play the game—for FREE!
You can also save Force Builds in the WARMACHINE app. These are your customized army configurations, saved and ready to play.
If you decide to subscribe to the WARMACHINE app, you’ll have access to a whole library of exciting content, with new articles added weekly as well as cloud storage that will allow you to access your Force Builds from any device you log in on.
Here’s what you can do in the WARMACHINE app:

name: Name
body: The Library in the WARMACHINE app gives you access to the rules of the game, reference documents, and content for subscribers like monthly fiction, new scenarios, setting lore, and an ongoing campaign.

name: Name
body: In WARMACHINE, every model or unit (a group of models) is represented by a series of stats and a list of abilities that determine what you can do with them in the game. Collectively, those stats and abilities are represented in the app by a model’s card. You can explore the stats and abilities of every WARMACHINE model and unit in the Cards section of the app.

name: Name
body:
Your force in WARMACHINE is a group of models you use when playing a tabletop battle. Every model and unit in WARMACHINE has a point cost. Forces are categorized by Army Point levels, which dictate how many points you have to spend on models and units in your force. The WARMACHINE app will calculate the number of points you have spent in assembling a force, and based on the point level you have selected, it will alert you if you have exceeded your point allowance or have in some other way made illegal selections in your Force Build.
The first step in building a force is selecting a warcaster or warlock to lead it. After that, you can add and customize the loadouts of warjacks or warbeasts, then spend your remaining points on solos and units as well as various attachments that upgrade the abilities of your units.

name: Name
caption: Once you have built a force, it will be saved in the app. You can save up to six Force Builds in the app without a subscription. If you wish to save more Force Builds, you’ll need to subscribe.

name: Name
body: Once you have built a force, you’re ready to start playing! After you find a worthy opponent, you’ll want share your Force Build through the app. To do this, select PLAY in the main app functions, and then select the saved Force Build you wish to use. From there, use the menu button in the upper-right to select SHARE OPPONENT QR CODE in order to create a QR code that your opponent can then scan to receive your Force Build. Your opponent will do the same, at which point you will select SCAN OPPONENT QR CODE to import your opponent’s information, allowing you to have visibility over all models in their force.

name: Name
body: The basics of WARMACHINE are easy to learn. The subtle interactions between models and the nuance of tactical opportunities in the game take time to master. The following training guide will walk you thought the fundamentals of turn sequence, movement, and combat to get you read to put your army on the tabletop in no time! (The full WARMACHINE MKIV rules are available in your WARMACHINE app library.)

name: Name
body:
In WARMACHINE, players take on the role of elite soldier-sorcerers known as warcasters or battle-shamans known as warlocks. Though warcasters are formidable, their strength lies in their magical ability to control warjacks, massive military automatons. No less powerful are the warlocks, whose strength lies in their parasitic synergy with savage warbeasts, monstrous creatures of flesh, blood, and bone. A WARMACHINE army is built around a warcaster and their battlegroup of warjacks or a warlock and their battlegroup of warbeasts. Squads of soldiers and support teams can further bolster a battlegroup’s combat capability.
This training guide is for players with armies led by warcasters playing in the Prime Arena.

name: Name
body: The MKIV edition includes two Arenas of play: Prime, which includes all new MKIV releases as well as limited model options for building armies from the pre-existing Legacy catalog; and Unlimited, which will allow all existing Legacy and new MKIV models to be playable.

name: Name
body: Grab 3–4 six-sided dice (we call a six-sided die a d6), a handful of tokens or small coins, and find a table at least 4’ x 4’ to play on and some gaming terrain to put on it. You’ll also need your models and an opponent!

name: Name
body: The first thing you’ll need to do is pick an encounter level and build a force. Encounter levels determine how many points you have to spend on models in your force. You can tap the "Build a Force″ button at the bottom of your screen and flip back and forth between this tutorial and your force at any time. For your first force, choose the 30-point Recon level and give your force a name.

name: Name
body:
Step 1 <indent=90>—<indent=130>Choose the Prime Arena, then MKIV.</indent></indent>
Step 2 <indent=90>—<indent=130>Choose your Army. </indent></indent>
Step 3 <indent=90>—<indent=130>Choose a Leader for your army. </indent></indent>
Step 4 <indent=90>—<indent=130>Spend Army Points to construct your force from the models available to your Army. </indent></indent>
Step 5 <indent=90>—<indent=130>Select Five Command Cards. </indent></indent>

name: Name
body: When you build a force, you get to choose five Command Cards, which provide tactical benefits during gameplay. You can play two per turn and you can only use each Command Card once.

name: Name
body: Before putting your models on the tabletop, each player should roll a die, and high roll goes first. Take turns placing 4–6 pieces of terrain to create your battlefield. After that, player one will place all the models in their force completely within their Deployment Zone, then player two will do the same. (Note: when you place a unit, put one model down, and then all other models in that unit must be placed within 2" of that first model.) Now you’re ready to play!

name: Name
body: Each WARMACHINE combatant is represented on the tabletop by a model. There are several different model types. This training guide will cover warcasters, warjacks, troopers, and solos.

name: Name
body: A warcaster is a tremendously powerful soldier-sorcerer with the ability to control a group of warjacks telepathically. Every warcaster has a replenishing reservoir of focus points they can spend to enhance their combat abilities and cast spells or allocate to individual warjacks to increase their fighting capabilities. All warcasters are unique characters. Warcasters are Leader models. During battle, a warcaster commands their battlegroup of warjacks in an effort to complete its objectives. A warcaster can use their focus points to enhance combat abilities and cast spells, or focus can be assigned to individual warjacks to increase their fighting abilities. A warcaster can also channel spells through warjacks equipped with arc nodes, effectively extending the range of its magical powers.

name: Name
body:
Warjacks are powered by steam technology and arcane science controlled by a warcaster. Also called ’jacks, these mighty creations are outfitted with a plethora of weaponry and equipment. A warcaster maintains telepathic contact with the ’jacks in their battlegroup and continually draws on a magical energy called focus. A crucial component of strategy is the warcaster’s management of focus to boost their warjacks’ abilities. Properly allocated, focus points can enhance a ’jack’s impressive combat power significantly!
Warjacks are Cohort models. They are classified according to base size: a light warjack has a medium base (40 mm), a heavy warjack has a large base (50 mm), a super heavy warjack has an extra-large base (80 mm), and a colossal has a huge base (120 mm).

name: Name
body: Solos are individuals who operate alone, such as assassins and snipers.

name: Name
body: A unit is a group of similarly trained and equipped warrior models—such as swordsmen, riflemen, and mechaniks—who operate together. All models in a unit are troopers. Models in units do not activate individually; instead, all members of the unit activate at the same time and progress through the steps of an activation together.

name: Name
body: Every model and unit has a unique profile in the WARMACHINE App called a Card. A model entry describes a model/unit’s statistics, spells, feats, and special rules.

name: Name
body: Model statistics, or stats, are a numerical representation of the model’s basic combat qualities: the higher the number, the better the stat. A stat bar presents model statistics in an easy-to-reference format. The abbreviation for each stat shows how it is referenced in the rules.

name: Name
caption: SPD, Speed—A model’s movement rate. A model moves up to its SPD in inches when making a full advance. AAT, Arcane Attack—A measure of a model’s potency in combat when casting offensive spells. A model uses its AAT when making arcane attack rolls. MAT, Melee Attack—A model’s skill with melee weapons such as swords and hammers or with natural weapons like fists and teeth. A model uses its MAT when making melee attack rolls. RAT, Ranged Attack—A model’s accuracy with ranged weapons such as guns and crossbows or thrown weapons like spears and knives. A model uses its RAT when making ranged attack rolls. DEF, Defense—A model’s ability to avoid being hit by an attack. A model’s size, quickness, skill, and even magical protection all contribute to its DEF. An attack roll must be equal to or greater than the target model’s DEF to score a hit against it. ARM, Armor—A model’s ability to resist being damaged. This resistance can come from natural resilience, worn armor, or even magical benefits. A model takes 1 damage point for every point a damage roll exceeds its ARM. ARC, Arcana—A measure of a model’s arcane power. Only models that cast spells using focus or fury points, such as warcasters and warlocks, have an ARC stat. Arc determines a model’s beginning focus or fury points. CTRL, Control Range—The radius of a warcaster’s control range. A control range is a circular area centered on the model with a radius that extends out from the edge of its base a number of inches equal to its current CTRL. Some spells and feats use the control range, noted as "CTRL," as their range or area of effect. A model is always considered to be in its own control range.

name: Name
body: Advantages are common special rules that many models have. A model’s advantages are marked as icons on its stat bar, along with its base size. You can find all of the Advantages icons in the Icon Reference Document in your app library, and by tapping on an Advantage, you can see its rules.

name: Name
body: Each warcaster has a unique and powerful special rule called a feat that can be used only once per game.

name: Name
body: A model can make a special action or a special attack during its Combat Action if it meets the requirements for using the special action or special attack.

name: Name
body: Some models have the ability to cast spells during their activation.

name: Name
body: Special rules on cards always overrule the basic rules of the game.

name: Name
body:
Many game situations, such as charging or making attacks, require a model to target another model. A model must have line of sight (LOS) to another model to target it. Simply put, having line of sight means a model can see another model. You can check your model’s line of sight at any time.
Line of sight can be blocked by other models with an equal or larger base size than the model LOS is being drawn to. Models in a unit do not block the line of sight of other models in their unit. Line of sight can also be blocked by terrain.

name: Name
body: On a model’s weapon stat bar, a sword icon denotes a melee weapon and a pistol icon denotes a ranged weapon. The entry for a model with two identical weapons has a single weapon stat bar with "×2" on the icon. A weapon’s stat bar lists only the stats that apply to its use. Those that are not applicable are marked with "—."

name: Name
caption: Sample Ranged Weapon Stat Bar for a Pair of Identical Weapons Sample Melee Weapon Stat Bar RNG, Range—The maximum distance in inches an attack can reach from its point of origin. ROF, Rate of Fire—The number of initial attacks a model can make with this ranged weapon during its activation. AOE, Area of Effect—When resolving a direct hit with an area-of-effect (AOE) weapon, this determines how many inches away from the target that other models will suffer blast damage. It also determines the potential number of models that can suffer blast damage from the attack. POW, Power—The value used when making damage rolls. A weapon or attack marked with a POW of "—" does not cause damage. Some special rules can affect a weapon’s POW. A weapon’s POW can never be reduced to less than 0. On an area-of-effect (AOE) weapon, the number after the "/" is the POW of blast damage inflicted by the weapon. L/R/H, Location—The weapon stat bars of warjacks indicate where their weapons are located: left arm (L), right arm (R), head (H), or superstructure (S).

name: Name
body: Weapon qualities are special rules that are marked as icons on a weapon’s stat block. You can find all of the Weapon Qualities icons in the Icon Reference Document in your app library, and by tapping on a Weapon Quality, you can see its rules.

name: Name
body: WARMACHINE battles are fought in a series of rounds. Each round, each player takes a turn in the order established during setup, beginning with the first player. Once the second player completes their turn, the current round ends. A new round then begins, starting with the first player again. Rounds continue until one player wins the game by destroying the opposing Leader, meeting the scenario objectives, or accepting the surrender of their opponent.

name: Name
body: A player’s turn has three phases: Maintenance, Control, and Activation. Maintenance Phase

name: Name
body: During the Maintenance Phase, perform the following steps in order: Remove all focus point tokens from your warjacks. (You won’t need to do this on your first turn because your warjacks don’t start the game with focus points on them.) Check for expiration of continuous effects on any models you control. After checking for expired continuous effects, resolve the effects of those that remain in play. Resolve all other effects that occur during the Maintenance Phase. Control Phase

name: Name
body: During the Control Phase, perform the following steps in order. Your warcaster replenishes their focus points. To replenish focus, a model gains focus points equal to its current ARC. Warjacks power up. Each warjack in a battlegroup that has a functional cortex and is within its controller’s control range gains 1 focus token. A warjack with a crippled cortex or no cortex at all cannot power up and does not gain this focus. Warcasters can allocate focus points to warjacks in their battlegroup that are in their control range. A model cannot allocate focus to a warjack with a crippled cortex. A warcaster can spend focus points to maintain its upkeep spells in play. If a model does not spend focus to maintain an upkeep spell, the spell expires, and its effects immediately end. Resolve all other effects that occur during the Control Phase. Activation Phase

name: Name
body: The Activation Phase is the major portion of a player’s turn when all models you control must be activated. Units and independent models are activated one at a time in the order you choose. A model cannot forfeit its activation unless allowed to do so by a special rule.

name: Name
body: Models either activate individually or as a unit. Only one model or unit can activate at a time. When a model activates, the activation is divided into its Normal Movement and its Combat Action. A model’s Normal Movement must be resolved before progressing to its Combat Action. After resolving its Combat Action, the model ends its activation. The active model must end its activation before another model or unit can be activated.

name: Name
body:
When a model or unit resolves its Normal Movement, it must choose one of the following options:
-Full advance
-Run
-Charge
-Aim

name: Name
body: Additionally, some models can choose to perform a power attack encompassing its Normal Movement and Combat Action such as a slam or trample power attack. Full Advance

name: Name
body: A model moves up to its SPD in inches when making a full advance, measured from the edge of its base. Advancing is intentional movement and not movement caused by involuntary effects, such as being pushed or slammed. A model’s base cannot pass over another model’s base while advancing. UNIT MOVEMENT

name: Name
body: When a unit advances as part of its Normal Movement—whether making a full advance, run, or charge—choose one trooper model in the unit to move. After determining that model’s movement, place the remaining troopers in that unit within 2" of that model. These models must be placed so that they have line of sight to the trooper that moved. Run

name: Name
body: When a model runs, it advances up to its current SPD plus 5". When a model uses its Normal Movement to run, it must forfeit its Combat Action before advancing, and its activation ends as soon as it completes its run movement. A model cannot cast a spell or use "any time" special rules after running. Unlike warrior models, a warjack must spend 1 focus point to use its Normal Movement to run. Charge

name: Name
body:
When a model charges, it rushes into melee range with a target and takes advantage of its momentum to make a more powerful melee strike.
A model requires line of sight to its target to charge. A charging model advances up to its current SPD plus 3" in a straight line in any direction that will bring its target into the range of one or more of its melee weapons.
The charging model stops if it contacts a model, an obstacle, or an obstruction.
A charging model ending its movement in melee range of its target must use its Combat Action to make either initial melee attacks or a special attack with a melee weapon against its target. If it advanced at least 3" and its charge attack hits, the damage roll is boosted, meaning another die is added to the roll. After resolving its charge attack, the charging model completes its Combat Action normally.
If a charging model moved less than 3", it must still target its charge target with its melee attack, but the damage roll is not boosted.
If a charging model ends its charge movement without its charge target in its melee range, it has failed its charge and ends its activation.

name: Name
body: A warjack must spend 1 focus point to use its Normal Movement to charge. UNIT CHARGES

name: Name
body: When a unit charges as part of its Normal Movement, select one unengaged model to move for the unit as described in Unit Movement. That model charges as described above. After the charging model completes its charge movement, place the other troopers in its unit within 2" of that model as normal. Troopers in the unit with enemy models in their melee range must use their Combat Actions to make either initial melee attacks or a special attack with a melee weapon. Troopers in the unit without an enemy model in their melee range must forfeit their Combat Actions. If the charging model ends its charge movement without its target in its melee range, it fails its charge and the unit’s activation ends after placing the troopers within 2" of the charging model. Aim

name: Name
body: If a model or unit choose not to move, it gains a +2 Aim bonus to every ranged attack roll it makes. Models do not gain this bonus while they are engaged.

name: Name
body: Models can also be moved without advancing as a result of being pushed or slammed or from other effects. Determine the distance a model moves in this way by measuring how far the leading edge of its base travels. Unintentional movement is not advancing.

name: Name
body:
During a model’s Combat Action, it can attack enemy targets. An attack roll determines if an attack hits its target. A damage roll determines how much damage an attack deals.
There are three main types of attacks: melee attacks, ranged attacks, and arcane attacks. Though a model cannot make both melee and ranged attacks in the same Combat Action, spellcasters with the ARCANE stat can make arcane attacks and melee or ranged attacks in the same activation.
If the target of an attack is in range, make an attack roll to determine if the attack hits. If the target is beyond range, the attack automatically misses.

name: Name
body: When measuring range, measure from the attacker’s base to the target’s base. If the distance is equal to or less than the range of the attack or special rule, the target is in range.

name: Name
body: A basic attack is an attack made with a weapon that is not a special attack, a power attack, or a chain attack.

name: Name
body: Special attacks are described on a model’s card.

name: Name
body: When making an attack, roll 2d6 and add the model’s appropriate stat for the attack type. Roll an additional die if the attack is boosted. Special rules and certain circumstances might modify the attack roll as well. Melee Attack Roll = 2d6 + MAT Ranged Attack Roll = 2d6 + RAT Arcane Attack Roll = 2d6 + AAT A model is directly hit by an attack if the attack roll against it equals or exceeds the model’s defense current (DEF). If the attack roll is less than the target’s DEF, the attack misses. If the attack hits and any two dice in the attack roll show the same number, it is a critical hit. Some attacks have additional effects when the attack is a critical hit. A die roll of all 1s is a miss. A roll of all 6s is a direct hit unless you are rolling only one die, regardless of the attacker’s MAT, RAT, AAT, or the target’s DEF.

name: Name
body:
Melee attacks include power attacks and attacks made with close combat weapons. A model using its Combat Action to make attacks with its melee weapons can make one initial attack with each of its melee weapons. Some models have special rules that allow additional melee attacks during their Combat Actions.
Warcasters and warjacks can spend focus points to make additional melee attacks.

name: Name
body: A model is engaged while it is within the melee range of an enemy model. A model that advances out of one or more enemy models’ melee ranges during its Normal Movement must forfeit its Combat Action. A model in a unit that was engaged prior to being placed as a result of its unit’s Normal Movement must also forfeit its Combat Action that activation unless it is placed within the melee range of any models that were previously engaging it. Power Attacks

name: Name
body:
Warjacks can use Power Attack advantages by spending 1 focus point.
-A model with the Headbutt Power Attack advantage can make headbutt power attacks.
-A model with the Slam Power Attack advantage can make slam power attacks.
-A model with a weapon with the Throw Power Attack weapon quality can make throw power attacks. A warjack cannot use a crippled weapon with the Throw Power Attack weapon quality to make a throw power attack.
-A model with the Trample Power Attack advantage can make trample power attacks.

name: Name
body: The full rules for Power Attacks can be found in the complete WARMACHINE rules doc.

name: Name
body:
Ranged attacks include attacks made with weapons such as firearms and spears. A model can make a ranged attack against any target in its line of sight and within its weapon’s range.
A model using its Combat Action to make attacks with its ranged weapons can make a number of initial attacks with each of its ranged weapons equal to the weapon’s rate of fire (ROF). Some models have special rules that allow additional ranged attacks during their activations.

name: Name
body:
Some attacks and special rules cause a model to become knocked down. While knocked down, a model cannot advance, make special actions, make attacks, cast spells, use feats, or be used to channel a spell. A knocked down model does not engage other models. A knocked down model has a base DEF of 5. A melee attack against a knocked down model automatically hits. A knocked down model does not block line of sight.
To stand up, a knocked down model forfeits either its Normal Movement or its Combat Action. A model that forfeits its Combat Action to stand can use its Normal Movement to make a full advance. When a model stands, it ceases to be knocked down.

name: Name
body: Some attacks and special rules cause models to become stationary. While stationary, a model cannot advance, make special actions, make attacks, cast spells, use feats, or be used to channel a spell. A stationary model does not engage other models. A stationary model has a base DEF of 5. A melee attack against a stationary model automatically hits.

name: Name
body: The most common modifiers affecting a model’s ranged attack roll are summarized here for easy reference. Where necessary, additional details can be found in the main rules document. Aim: A model that uses its Normal Movement to aim receives a +2 bonus to every ranged attack roll it makes this activation. A model cannot gain this bonus while engaged. Cloud Effect: A model inside a cloud effect gains concealment. Concealment: A model with concealment gains +2 DEF against ranged and arcane attack rolls. Huge-based models cannot gain the DEF bonus from concealment. Cover and concealment bonuses are not cumulative. Cover: A model with cover gains +4 DEF against ranged and arcane attacks. Huge-based models cannot gain the DEF bonus from cover. Cover and concealment are not cumulative. Elevation Bonus: Large, medium and small-based models gains +2 DEF against ranged and arcane attack rolls made by models on lower elevations. Extra-large and huge-based models cannot gain the DEF bonus for elevation. Engaged Attacker: A model engaged by one or more enemy models can only make ranged attacks targeting enemy models engaging it. Additionally, while engaged, a model cannot gain the bonus for aiming. Knocked Down Target: While knocked down, a model has its base DEF reduced to 5. Target in Melee: An extra-large, large, medium, or small-based model in melee gains +4 DEF against ranged and arcane attacks. Huge-based models cannot gain the target in melee DEF bonus. Stationary Target: While stationary, a model has its base DEF reduced to 5.

name: Name
body: Terrain features, spells, and other effects can make it more difficult to hit a model with a ranged or arcane attack. A model with concealment, either granted by being within 1̋ of a terrain feature that provides concealment in relation to its attacker or from another effect, gains +2 DEF against non-spray ranged and arcane attack rolls. Examples of concealment-granting terrain features include low hedges and bushes. A model with cover, granted either by being within 1̋ of a terrain feature that provides cover in relation to its attacker or from another effect, gains +4 DEF against non-spray ranged and arcane attack rolls. Examples of cover-granting terrain features include stone walls, giant boulders, and buildings. Huge-based models cannot gain the DEF bonuses from concealment or cover. Area-of-Effect (AOE) Attacks

name: Name
body:
An area of effect attack (or AOE attack) is an attack that has the potential to hit other models in addition to its target. When an AOE attack directly hits its target, resolve the attack against the target as normal. Then, when an AOE attack hits its target, additional models (a number equal to the AOE value of the attack) that are closest to the target are hit. (These models need to be within a number of inches of the target equal to the AOE value of the attack.) They suffer a blast damage roll from the attack. If multiple models are equally distant from the target, randomize between them to determine which models suffer the blast damage.
AOE attacks have two POWs listed under their stat profiles. The number before the "/" is the POW of a direct hit against a target model. The number after the "/" is the POW of the attack’s blast damage.
When an AOE attack misses and the target was within the attack’s RNG, the target suffers a blast damage roll.
When an attack roll for an AOE results in a critical hit, every model hit by the AOE suffers the critical effect.

name: Name
body: Spray Attacks

name: Name
body:
Spray attacks are devastating short-ranged attacks that can have the ability to hit several models. A spray attack follows all normal targeting rules. When making a spray attack, measure the full range of the spray, centering it on the target model’s base. Every model whose base this line intersects with has a chance of being hit by the attack. A model cannot be hit by the attack if the attacker’s line of sight to it is completely blocked to the model by terrain. Make a separate attack and damage roll against each model that may have been hit by the attack, including the original target.
Spray attacks ignore concealment, cover, and Stealth.

name: Name
body: A model can make an arcane attack targeting any model in the spell’s range that is in its line of sight. Arcane attacks do not receive an attack bonus for aiming but are otherwise affected by all Ranged Attack Modifiers.

name: Name
body: To determine how much damage is caused by an attack, roll 2d6 and add the Power (POW) of the weapon or spell. A boosted damage roll adds an additional die to this roll. Damage Roll = 2d6 + POW Compare this total against the Armor (ARM) of the model suffering the damage. That model takes 1 damage point for every point that the damage roll exceeds its ARM. A model cannot suffer more damage than it has damage boxes.

name: Name
body: The total amount of damage a model can suffer before being disabled is noted by damage boxes on its card. A model is disabled once all of its damage boxes are marked. Models without boxes are disabled after taking 1 damage point. Damage Grids

name: Name
body:
Warjacks have damage grids consisting of six columns of damage boxes labeled with the numbers 1 through 6. When a model with a damage grid suffers damage, roll a d6 to determine which column takes the damage. Starting with the uppermost unmarked box in that column and working down, mark one damage box per damage point taken. Once a column is full, continue recording damage in the next column to the right that contains an unmarked damage box. If all the damage boxes in column 6 are marked, continue recording damage in column 1 or the next column that contains an unmarked damage box. Continue filling columns as required until every damage point taken has been recorded.
When a rule specifically states a model suffers damage to the "first" box of a given system (see "Warjack Damage Key" callout), find the lowest numbered column on the model’s card that has an unmarked damage box for that system and mark the uppermost unmarked damage box of that system.

name: Name
body: Warjack Damage Key On a warjack’s damage grid, the following letters represent the warjack’s systems: A: Arc Node C: Cortex G: Power Field Generator H: Head M: Movement F: Front weapon system L: Left Arm weapon system R: Right Arm weapon system CRIPPLING SYSTEMS

name: Name
body: The letters on a warjack’s damage grid correspond to its systems. When recording damage, mark blank boxes as well as those containing system labels to record the correct amount of damage. When all the boxes corresponding to a system are marked, the system is crippled. The effects of crippled systems are as follows: -Crippled Arc Node: The model loses the Arc Node advantage. -Crippled Cortex: The model loses any focus points on it and cannot gain or spend focus points for any reason. -Crippled Head: The model loses any special rules, including advantages, associated with its head system. When a warjack with a crippled Head (H) system makes an attack with a weapon mounted in its head, treat it as an attack with a crippled weapon system (see below). -Crippled Power Field Generator: A model with a crippled Power Field Generator cannot spend focus points to reduce damage it suffers. -Crippled Movement: The model has its base DEF changed to 5. It cannot run, charge, or make slam or trample power attacks.

name: Name
body: -Weapon System: The model rolls one fewer die on attack and damage rolls with weapons in the crippled location. Additionally, a model cannot use weapons in a crippled location to make power attacks or special attacks. If a weapon in the crippled location has the Buckler or Shield weapon quality, the model loses the ARM bonus for that quality while the location is crippled.

name: Name
body: If 1 or more damage points are removed from a crippled system, the system is no longer crippled.

name: Name
body:
A model is disabled when all its damage boxes are marked or, if it does not have damage boxes, when it suffers 1 damage point. When a model is disabled, immediately resolve any effects triggered by being disabled. If 1 or more damage points are removed from a disabled model, it is no longer disabled.
After resolving any effects triggered by being disabled, if the model is still disabled, it is considered to be boxed. When a model is boxed, resolve any effects triggered by being boxed. After resolving any effects triggered by being boxed, if the model is still boxed, it is destroyed, triggering any relevant effects. Remove the destroyed model from the table.

name: Name
body: A warcaster is a Leader model and has the following special rules.

name: Name
body:
This model has an Arcana stat (ARC) that determines how many focus points it gains each turn. During your Control Phase, this model replenishes its focus points so that it has a number equal to its current ARC. This model begins the game with a number of focus points equal to its ARC. Unless otherwise stated, a model can spend focus points only during its activation. A model with Focus Manipulation can:
-make one additional melee attacks for each focus spent during its Combat Action.
-spend 1 focus point to boost any of its attack or damage rolls during its activation. Boosting must be declared before rolling any dice for the roll.

name: Name
body: This model can control one or more warjacks. This model and the ’jacks it controls are collectively referred to as a battlegroup. This model can allocate focus points to warjacks in its battlegroup and can channel spells through warjacks in its battlegroup with the Arc Node advantage. Power Up

name: Name
body: Warjacks are empowered by the mere presence of their controlling warcaster on the battlefield. During the Control Phase, each warjack with a functional cortex in a battlegroup that is in its controller’s control range gains 1 focus point. Allocating Focus Points

name: Name
body: A battlegroup controller can allocate focus points to the warjacks in its battlegroup during your Control Phase. A warjack must be in its battlegroup controller’s control range to be allocated focus, though it need not be in its line of sight. A warjack can have no more than 3 focus points at any time, and a warjack with a crippled cortex cannot be allocated focus.

name: Name
body: Warcaster armor is perhaps the most sophisticated blend of magic and mechanics to be found anywhere. Besides its seemingly impossible strength, this armor creates a magical field to surround and protect the warcaster from damage that would rend a normal individual to pieces. At any time during its activation, this model can spend focus points to remove damage it has suffered. For each focus point spent this way, the model can remove 1 damage point. Reinforcing the Power Field

name: Name
body: When a model with the Power Field special rule would suffer damage, it can immediately spend up to 1 focus point to reduce the damage it would suffer by 5. The model is still considered to have suffered damage even if the damage is reduced to 0 or less.

name: Name
body: This model can cast spells by paying the COST of the spells in focus points.

name: Name
body: Warjacks are independent Cohort models. All warjacks have the Construct advantage and are not living models. All warjacks have the following special rules.

name: Name
body: Warjacks can gain focus. A warjack can have no more than 3 focus points at any time. A warjack cannot gain or spend focus while its Cortex system is crippled.

name: Name
body:
Warjacks may spend 1 focus to do any of the following:
-make an additional melee attack as part of its Combat Action.
-boost an attack or damage rolls during its activation. Boosting must be declared before rolling any dice for the roll.
-run or charge during its Normal Movement.
-make a power attack.

name: Name
body:
Some models have the ability to cast spells during their activations. Warcasters cast spells by paying the spell’s COST in focus points. Models with Magic Ability cast spells by making a special action or special attack.
A spell’s point of origin is the model casting the spell or the model through which the spell is channeled.

name: Name
body:
A spell can target any model in the spellcaster’s line of sight and within the spell’s RNG. Many spells can target only certain types of models, such as warjacks or enemy troopers. Such restrictions are noted in the spell’s description.
Offensive spells can only target enemy models and require a successful arcane attack to hit.
Non-offensive spells can only target friendly models and do not require a roll to take effect.

name: Name
title: Casting a Spell with Magic Ability

name: Name
body: Models with the Magic Ability special rule can cast the spells listed on their card as special attacks or special actions.

name: Name
body: A model with the ARC stat can cast any number of spells during its activation for which it can pay the COST. A spell can be cast multiple times per activation if the COST can be paid. A model can cast spells by spending focus points at any time during its activation.

name: Name
body: Spells cast using focus points are defined by the following six statistics. If a stat is listed as "*," the spell does not use the stat in a normal way and contains special rules relating to that aspect of the spell. COST—The number of focus points that must be spent to cast the spell. RNG, Range—The distance in inches the spell can be cast from the spellcaster to the target. A RNG of "SELF" indicates the spell can target only the model casting it. A RNG of "CTRL" indicates the spell can target any model in the spellcaster’s control range. Remember, the spellcaster needs line of sight to a model to target it. AOE, Area of Effect—When resolving a direct hit with an offensive spell with an AOE, this determines how many inches away from the target that other models will suffer blast damage. It also determines the potential number of models that can suffer blast damage from the attack. Any spell with an AOE of "CTRL" is centered on the spellcaster and affects models in its control range.

name: Name
body: POW, Power—This damage is magical. A spell with POW "—" does not inflict damage. When resolving a direct hit with an offensive spell with an AOE, the number after the "/" is the POW of blast damage inflicted by the weapon. Duration—Determines how long the spell effect remains in play. Spells generally have a duration of one turn (TURN) or one round (RND), are upkeep spells (UP), or have no duration past the resolution of their effect. Spells with a duration of "—" remain in play only long enough to resolve their effects. An upkeep spell remains in play if its spellcaster spends 1 focus point to maintain it during its controller’s Control Phase. OFF, Offensive (Yes/No)—Determines whether the spell is an arcane attack.

name: Name
body:
Upkeep spells are spells that can be maintained from round to round. During your Control Phase, your models can spend focus to keep their upkeep spells in play. Each upkeep spell requires 1 focus point for its upkeep every round. If focus is not spent to maintain one of your upkeep spells during your Control Phase, the spell expires.
A spellcaster can have only one instance of each specific upkeep spell in play at a time, but it can maintain any number of different upkeep spells simultaneously if it spends enough focus points to do so. A model or unit can have only one friendly and one enemy upkeep spell in play on it at a time. If another upkeep spell is cast on a model or unit that already has one from the same side—friendly or enemy—the older upkeep spell expires and is replaced by the newer one when the affected model is hit by the spell. For a unit, the older upkeep spell expires even if only a single model in the unit is affected by the new upkeep spell. Likewise, an upkeep spell on one model expires if any model in its unit is affected by a new upkeep spell from the same side.

name: Name
body:
A model can recast any of its upkeep spells already in play. If this happens, the spell’s previous casting expires when the COST of the new casting is paid.
When a spellcaster is destroyed or removed from play, its upkeep spells expire.

name: Name
body:
Some models, known as channelers, can act as passive relays for spells and extend their effective range. The most common channelers are warjacks with the Arc Node advantage. A spellcaster can cast spells through any channeler in its battlegroup that is also within its control range. The spellcaster is still the model casting the spell and, if the spell is offensive, is the attacker, but the channeler becomes the spell’s point of origin. This means that eligible targets and the spell’s range are measured from the channeler and that the channeling model must have line of sight to the spell’s target. Channeling a spell does not require the spellcaster to have line of sight to either the channeler or the spell’s target.
A channeler that is stationary, knocked down, or engaged by an enemy model cannot channel spells. A channeler can be the target of a non-offensive spell it channels, but a spell with a RNG of "SELF" cannot be channeled.
Make an arcane attack for a channeled offensive spell normally. The spellcaster can spend focus to boost die rolls.

name: Name
body:
Once you have gotten familiar with the basics, continue your warcaster journey with the full WARMACHINE MKIV rules available in the app library.
Good luck, Warcaster!

name: Warcaster Training Guide - Chapter 1 Welcome to WARMACHINE and the Warcaster Training Guide
